title: late-release-night-handback-scratch
content:
Scratchpad: late-release overnight handback comms and all-team crib notes

TL;DR
- We are doing a constrained late release (non-blocking) tonight 23:00–02:00 PT. Primary goals: small feature push, DB migration flag-on for non-critical table, and a config toggle for routing fallback.
- Night shift will own 23:00–06:00; handback to daytime SRE at 06:00 with a short summary and open tickets.
- This doc = my personal talking bullets + Qs to prep for quick all-team ping and async postmortem template.

Purpose / audience
- Purpose: make handoff predictable, reduce wakeups, and set internal expectations.
- Audience: oncall SRE, product engineer on call, program manager, and “ops-watch” list (small group).

Release window & scope
- Start: 2026-02-24 23:00 PT
- End / handback: target 2026-02-25 06:00 PT
- Scope: feature flag for routing fallback (safe-by-default), non-blocking DB migration (migrate in background, toggle later), infra config tweak to batching defaults (rollout 10% then 100%).
- Risk level: low–medium; main risk = unexpected latency bump due to batching changes.

Key messages (short pings)
- Slack ping (ops-watch): "Starting late release now (23:00 PT). Night team owning. Expect brief performance monitoring; will call for help if we see >15% tail latency increase. Handback at 06:00 PT. Tickets: OPS-4721, DEPLOY-989."
- All-hands microline (if asked): "Small scoped deploy tonight to reduce routing errors and enable safer fallbacks; we expect no user-visible downtime and will monitor closely."

All-hands / exec crib lines (2-3 sentences)
- "We're shipping a modest, safety-first change tonight to harden routing behavior during peak failure modes. We do not expect customer impact; SRE will monitor and will escalate to the oncall lead if anything deviates from our SLOs."

Anticipated Q&A (short answers)
- Q: Will customers see downtime?
  A: No planned downtime; all changes are feature-flagged and can be rolled back within minutes.
- Q: What are rollback criteria?
  A: Any sustained >10% P95 increase for 15+ minutes OR error-rate spike >0.5% above baseline triggers immediate rollback and paging.
- Q: Who pages?
  A: Night oncall first, then oncall lead (pager), then SRE manager if uncontained.

Oncall / escalation flow (notes)
- Night SRE (primary) monitors dashboards: latency, error-rate, token-per-second, GPU queue length.
- Use Slack rollout channel + #ops-rotation-thread. If paging: call sequence -> pager -> phone for oncall lead.

Handback checklist (to send at 06:00 PT)
- Summary: start/end time, tickets opened, feature-flag state, any degraded metrics and current status.
- Artifacts to attach: traces/screenshots, small perf diff table, list of actions taken.
- TODO: confirm app-level config values (batch-size, idle-timeout) are recorded in deploy notes.

Quick runbook extract (to pin in channel)
- If P95 rises >10% for 10m -> flip batching flag back to previous and watch 10m window.
- If errors spike -> enable fallback routing (manual toggle path), notify product, and start rollback flow.

Comm templates (copy/paste)
- Start ping (ops-watch): "Starting late deploy (OPS-4721, DEPLOY-989) — night SRE owning. Monitoring for latency and errors. Will post handback at 06:00 PT or earlier if rollback."
- Handback ping: "HANDOFF: release complete (23:00–06:00 PT). Flags: fallback=on, DB-migration=running background, batch-config=100% -> notes: saw transient P95 +8% at 00:12 for ~6m; rolled back batch toggle at 00:20. Open tickets: OPS-4721 (investigate P95 spike), DEPLOY-989 (DB migration)."
- Escalation ping (if needed): "ALERT: sustained latency >10% P95 for 15m. Paging oncall lead and initiating rollback per runbook."

Open questions / unknowns (items to resolve before start)
- Who’s explicitly on call for product rollback (name/phone)? (ask PM: Inez)
- Confirm snapshot cadence for DB before background migration step (ops runbook).
- Do we want extra synthetic checks for embeddings endpoints? (embedding infra sensitive to batching)

To do (personal)
- Drop a short runbook link in pinned channel (before 22:45).
- Confirm night SRE has admin toggle permissions (I emailed Maya; need confirmation).
- Prepare a 1-paragraph handback template in a Google doc for quick paste.

Notes to self / talking points to practice
- Emphasize safety-first and quick rollback ability.
- Keep messages short — ops channel only for payload; use thread for detailed logs.
- When oncall pages, rely on pager+SMS fallback, do not escalate via DM-only.

Postmortem skeleton (async)
- Title: late-release-2026-02-24
- Time window: 23:00–06:00 PT
- Summary, impact (none/partial), timeline, root cause(s), remediation, follow-ups (owner + ETA).

Random low-priority notes (brain dump)
- Consider moving batch-config ramp to canary-by-region next time.
- Add a quick synthetic that hits _routing-fallback_ path as smoke test.

End of scratchpad — will tidy into a short pinned comms note if night starts smoothly.
